maya (Support): FYI escalating a customer miller/AcmeProd report — they say a small prompt tweak that used to be fine now returns completely different format. Started after yesterday's canary rollout of gptx-3.2-quant-v2 kernel changes. Requesting engineering triage. (customer provided request_id:req_0a9f2b)

aj (Eng-runtime): thanks — can you paste the exact prompt + minimal repro? any request IDs we can chase in logs?

maya (Support): Copied from the customer. They say the only change was adding a trailing period to a slot in the template. Before (worked):

```
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: Convert the following data to JSON.
Template: name: {{name}}
age: {{age}}
Input: "Alice, 29"
```

Model response (old):

```
{"name":"Alice","age":29}
```

After small change (breaks): they added a trailing period to the Input field value — just "Alice, 29." (note the extra dot)

```
System: You are a helpful assistant.
User: Convert the following data to JSON.
Template: name: {{name}}
age: {{age}}
Input: "Alice, 29."
```

Model response (new):

```
Alice is 29 years old.
```

So the model now returns a prose sentence instead of the JSON payload. Customer says this used to be robust and cropping punctuation didn't matter. Happened after yesterday's canary 2024-11-02 rollout (canary group ~15% traffic). Request id examples: req_0a9f2b, req_0aa9c3 for same flow.

aj (Eng-runtime): ugh. two quick hypotheses: 1) tokenizer/normalization change in the new kernel or compilation path caused different tokenization of trailing punctuation leading to different decoding. 2) system prompt/role prefix concatenation order changed so template detection fails and model falls back to generic completion.

diYa (Eng-ML): (note: diya spelled Diya) can you confirm which model variant they hit? gptx-3.2-quant-v2 vs gptx-3.2-fp16? If the rollout included a compiled kernel that altered the top-k/top-p behavior or temperature scheduling for short inputs, it could change the greedy behavior for punctuation.

maya (Support): telemetry shows the customer hit gptx-3.2-quant-v2 on both requests. I pulled the canary rollout PR: https://internal/repo/rollouts/PR-8276 — it includes a quantized-kernel change and a small change to prompt truncation logic to avoid exceeding model window.

carlos (Product): how many customers hit this regression? Is it isolated to template-type prompts or more widespread? We need to assess rollback risk vs cost of pinning.

nina (SRE): our error metrics don't show an increase in 5xx, but the quality regression alert count spiked: evals/quality/regression-alerts shows +42 alerts correlated with gptx-3.2-quant-v2 since 11/02 03:00 UTC. Latency slightly improved for quant-v2 but quality QA failures up.

aj (Eng-runtime): request: can someone provide a minimal curl repro that replicates the bad behavior so we can run locally and bisect? I'll try to reproduce locally against both quant-v2 and the previous compiled kernel. Also need the exact request headers (system prompt injection, max_tokens, temperature).

maya (Support): customer supplied a minimal curl. Putting here:

```bash
curl -s -X POST \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{
    "model":"redwood/gptx-3.2-quant-v2",
    "input": "System: You are a helpful assistant.\nUser: Convert the following data to JSON.\nTemplate: name: {{name}}\nage: {{age}}\nInput: \"Alice, 29.\"",
    "max_tokens": 60,
    "temperature": 0.0
  }'
```

Response: plain text "Alice is 29 years old." (not JSON).

aj (Eng-runtime): thanks. I'll run this against the canary image and the previous image and diff logits if needed.

diYa (Eng-ML): while aj runs that, quick check: could be related to decoding constraints or post-processing A/B — earlier we introduced a fallback for 'structured-output' templates that relied on a prefix match. If prompt normalization now strips the trailing punctuation before the template recognizer runs, the recognizer might fail and we hit unconstrained generation.

aj (Eng-runtime): reproducer run: on my laptop with quant-v2 image I get prose output; with quant-v1 (previous) I get JSON. So reproducible. I'll dump tokenization of the input for both binaries.

aj (Eng-runtime): tokenization diff (excerpt):

```
quant-v1 tokens: [  60, 1023, 7, 9001, ... , 12 ]
quant-v2 tokens: [ 60, 1023, 7, 9001, ... , 102 ]  # trailing dot produced different final token grouping
```

aj (Eng-runtime): interesting — trailing '.' becomes part of previous token in v2 causing model to see a slightly different last token which changes top candidates. That matches the customer symptom. Could be tokenizer mapping change in the new compiled kernel.

diYa (Eng-ML): if token boundaries moved, that explains brittle prompt-template matching. Our structured-output detector does substring checks on raw token boundary sequences in some paths — that's a brittle assumption. We should remove token-boundary reliant heuristics. For immediate mitigation we can snapshot the tokenizer mapping used by quant-v1 and pin quant-v2 to use the old mapping or run a compatibility mapping layer in the prompt pipeline.

carlos (Product): immediate ask: can we hotfix the canary to disable the new tokenizer mapping and push a compatibility shim? If not, rollback canary to quant-v1 for all customers with structured templates.

nina (SRE): we can do a canary rollback. Deploy-bot, can you rollback PR-8276 canary group? We'll need a short incident note for customers affected and patch notes.

deploy-bot: Rolling back canary for rollout PR-8276 across eu-west-1 and us-east-1 canary groups. Start: 1745001502. ETA 3m.

maya (Support): I've informed the customer that we're investigating, provided a temporary workaround: normalize input by removing trailing punctuation in the template (e.g., strip trailing periods before sending). They will test, but they want a permanent fix.

aj (Eng-runtime): followups for eng-runtime:
- add compatibility tokenizer mapping to prompt preprocess that maps quant-v2 tokens to quant-v1 equivalents for a short window. owner: aj.
- add unit test covering template detection with punctuation variants. owner: aj.

diYa (Eng-ML): followups for eng-ml:
- audit structured-output detector for token-boundary reliance; implement robust string-based fallback. owner: diya.
- run model-compare suite across 500 templated prompts to detect sensitivity regressions. owner: diya.

carlos (Product): product followups:
- notify top affected customers and prepare rollback communication. owner: carlos.
- evaluate if we should change release gating for tokenizer/kernel changes. owner: carlos.

nina (SRE): SRE followups:
- monitoring: add an anomaly alert for spikes in structured-output mismatches (already added). owner: nina.
- coordinate rollback and confirm metrics return to baseline. owner: nina.

maya (Support): customer said workaround (strip punctuation) restores JSON for their flows; they're ok with rollback if we can confirm timeline. I'll keep them updated.

aj (Eng-runtime): quick notes: I'll push a patch to inject a tokenizer compatibility mapping into the request pipeline (low-risk) and run canary smoke tests. If that doesn't pass fast, we'll complete the rollback.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback complete. End: 1745001620. Details: https://internal/deploys/PR-8276/rollback/1745001620

maya (Support): marking as escalated -> resolved (temporary rollback). I'll file a follow-up doc for permanent fix and link to this thread. tag @eng-runtime @eng-ml for postmortem. :white_check_mark:

aj (Eng-runtime): filing a short postmortem/patch PR to address tokenizer compatibility and increasing pre-release tests for template sensitivity. PR-8290 created.

diYa (Eng-ML): I'll queue regression-run and update the model evaluation dashboard to show template-sensitivity as a tracked metric.

carlos (Product): thanks all. let's aim to have a compatibility patch or robust detector in the next 72h.

nina (SRE): closing the incident timeline once regression alert count returns to baseline; tracking in incidents/1745001234.

maya (Support): closing customer loop now. will reopen if the customer sees recurrence after stable rollout.

[END THREAD]
